perspective:
**Vincent Chinana’s available information:**

- He knows Patrick Guzman is his long-time friend since their teenage years. They share a bond over blue-collar work and often collaborate, combining Vincent’s mechanical skills with Patrick’s construction expertise.
- At the diner, Vincent hears Patrick is considering a new construction venture to expand his business. Patrick says it seems like a good opportunity, that he thinks it’s worth the risk, but that he is still weighing his options. Vincent tells Patrick he has heard it is risky, worries about financial security, and suggests reconsidering or delaying until Patrick gathers more information. Patrick thanks him and says he will think it over.
- Later, Vincent notices Patrick avoiding detailed discussions about the investment. At Patrick’s construction site, Vincent tells Patrick he feels Patrick is not telling him everything and that he feels betrayed. Patrick apologizes, says it is complicated, says he did not want to worry Vincent, admits he should have been more open, and offers to explain everything.
- At Vincent’s garage, Vincent hears Patrick describe the investment troubles as serious and says Patrick might lose a significant amount if it does not turn around soon. Vincent offers to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses. Patrick thanks him and expresses gratitude for his support.
- A month later, at a coffee shop, Vincent has learned new information indicating the venture might actually turn a profit. He tells Patrick this. Patrick says it is starting to look up and that he is relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologizes for doubting him earlier and proposes a joint venture. Patrick agrees, and they plan to work out the details.
- At Vincent’s house, Vincent and Patrick are optimistic about their joint venture. Vincent says their combined skills can make it a success and proposes drafting a business plan carefully. Patrick agrees and says they should cover all their bases.

Vincent’s own actions/feelings include: being worried about Patrick’s risk, feeling betrayed when Patrick avoided details, offering financial help, apologizing for doubting Patrick, becoming optimistic, and initiating/agreeing to the joint venture and business planning. He does not have access to Patrick’s private thoughts, unspoken reasoning, or any events beyond what he directly observed or was told.
